did_you_know.text: Did you know? King Zedekiah sent two messengers to Jeremiah—Pashhur son of Malchiah and Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest—to ask for a word from the Lord.
Did you know? Zedekiah’s messengers asked Jeremiah to pray for Jerusalem and hope that the Lord would perform a miracle for them and remove the Babylonian army from them.
Did you know? The Lord announced that the weapons of war used by Jerusalem’s defenders would be turned against them and gathered inside the city instead of being used against its enemies.
Did you know? Contrary to the king’s expectation of help, the Lord said that He Himself would fight against Jerusalem with an outstretched hand, a mighty arm, and great anger.
Did you know? The punishment described in the chapter would affect both the people and the animals in the city, and they would die from a severe plague.
Did you know? After the plague, sword, and famine, Zedekiah, his servants, and the survivors in the city would be handed over to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and to those seeking their lives.
Did you know? Jeremiah presented the people with two options called “the way of life” and “the way of death”—a decisive choice that would determine Jerusalem’s fate.

Did you know? According to Jeremiah, those who remained in Jerusalem would die by the sword, famine, or plague, while those who went out and surrendered to the Chaldeans would live and save their lives.
Did you know? The chapter says that the Lord had set His face against Jerusalem for harm and not for good, and that the city would be handed over to the king of Babylon and burned with fire.

Did you know? Alongside the prophecy of destruction, Jeremiah gave the house of David a clear moral command: administer justice every morning and rescue the one who has been robbed from the hand of the oppressor.
